items.claim: engineHarness keeps one timer slot, so a second engine timer replaces or cancels the scheduler's pass
engineHarness.run overshoots a duration that isn't a multiple of 25 ms
items.note: Same file and same `run` loop as the timer fix, so it went into that commit.

items.claim: Repeated `connect` records a duplicate edge, and a targeted `disconnect` removes only one copy
A targeted `disconnect` that throws still marks the node disconnected
`dueToEnd` ignores the start offset and playback rate, and `start` drops its `duration` argument
items.note: `start` now also throws a RangeError for a negative time, offset or duration, as the spec does.

items.claim: `resume`/`suspend` on a closed fake context reopen it
items.note: `close` on a closed context now rejects too.

items.claim: `createBuffer` accepts any sample rate, and `getChannelData` returns undefined for a channel the buffer doesn't have
The fake analyser's canned bytes depend on the destination array's length, not the bin count
`FakeWorker._fail` fires after `terminate`
`stubWorkerGlobals().restore` unstubs every global in the test, not just its own
renderEngineStereo hangs when `later.run` throws, and its `suspend` rejects unhandled when `later.at` is out of range
items.note: I made the strict call: a `later.at` the render can't pause at throws a RangeError. That covers a time outside the render, or inside the first quantum when worklet voices hold it. It is recorded in `docs/unruled.md` in 630ddbe5e5. A `later.run` that throws now lets the render finish and then rejects with its error.

items.claim: Tests in `graph/sources.test.ts`, `graph/processors.test.ts` and `graph/wrapper.test.ts` built buffers at 10 Hz and 100 Hz, which a browser refuses. They now build them at 48 kHz with the same durations
engineHarness keeps one timer slot, so another timer can replace or clear the scheduler's pass
items.note: Both harnesses now share a new `fakeTimers` that gives each timer its own handle.

items.claim: engineHarness.run moves the clock past the time it is given, e.g. 25 ms for `run(10)`
dueToEnd ignores the start offset and playback rate
items.note: It now also counts detune, never ends a source at rate 0, and handles a negative rate.

items.claim: A repeated connect records a duplicate edge, and one disconnect leaves it in place
A targeted disconnect that throws still sets `disconnected`
getChannelData returns undefined for a channel the buffer doesn't have
createBuffer accepts a sample rate of 0, giving an Infinity duration (B, side note)
items.note: The fake now refuses a rate that is not positive and finite. It still takes rates below the spec's 3000 Hz floor, because `graph/sources.test.ts`, `graph/processors.test.ts` and `graph/wrapper.test.ts` use 100 Hz buffers so a second is 100 frames. Enforcing the full range broke 16 of their tests.

items.claim: resume, suspend and close on a closed context succeed and reopen it
The analyser's function spec gets the read length instead of the bin count
items.note: The existing test that relied on the old length now sets `fftSize = 8`.

items.claim: stubWorkerGlobals' restore removes every global the test stubbed
FakeWorker._fail still fires on a terminated worker
The fake worklet node keeps its edges after disconnect, records no back-edge, and connect returns undefined
items.note: It is now built on `node()`, so it has a FakeNode's edges.

items.claim: Failing the fake addModule before anything awaits it causes an unhandled rejection
engineHarness's clearTimer clears whatever is armed, whatever the handle
powerSpectrum accepts a frame size that is not a power of two
rmsEnvelope hangs on a window of 0 or less
items.note: It throws RangeError, and a fractional window does too. I didn't run the pre-fix test because it would hang; the loop that never advances is plain in the code.

items.claim: renderEngineStereo's `later` suspend collides with the worklet hold, and its failure is dropped
items.note: With worklet voices, a `later.at` inside the first render quantum now runs during the first hold. A `later.at` outside the render throws RangeError, and a failed pause fails the render. This one is untested here: its test is a browser test.
